$meta.readThisFirst: ⚠️ TWO HEADER COMPONENTS — POSSIBLY THREE — AND IT IS NOT SETTLED WHICH IS CANONICAL. This contract measures table_head 26938:61726 / table_cell 26938:61725 from section 26955:66556, which the owner identified as where the table is defined. But the document-level copy-from stylesheet (Universal Html Rules/02-components/table.css) builds from a DIFFERENTLY NAMED, differently numbered header: 'Head / Tiltes for tables' 5865:162, which it calls canonical. Both measure 34px, so this is not a size conflict — they are separate components. And this section's OWN sample layout (27002:78668) instantiates nodes named 'Head / Tiltes for tables', i.e. the stylesheet's source rather than its own table_head set. With 'X-Head old' already formally dead per that stylesheet, that is potentially three header components in one Figma file. A feature session cannot be expected to pick correctly — this is a strong candidate for why table builds have not matched the design system. RESOLVE THIS FIRST. Also: until 2026-08-25 there was no table contract here at all while the repo's only table stylesheet (src/styles/3-components/_tables.scss, 33 lines) had zero height declarations, so tools reading GitHub for table geometry got nothing. And note Figma prints WRONG padding fallbacks on the head cell (9 where spacing/md is 8, 1 where spacing/none is 0) while printing the same tokens correctly on the data cell — bind the token, never the printed fallback.

componentSets.name: table_head
componentSets.figmaDescription: Table header cell component. Styled for the header row with distinct background and typography treatment. 1 variant: type=Default. Composable with table_cell to build full data tables. Part of the Table component family.

componentSets.name: table_cell
componentSets.figmaDescription: Table body data cell component. Standard cell for table rows displaying data values. 1 variant: type=Default. Composable with table_head to build full data tables. Part of the Table component family.

supporting.name: column_actions
supporting.note: Structure and sizes only — token bindings NOT read.

supporting.name: sample-layout_table
supporting.structure: 3 x table_column, each = 1 head (34px) + table_data frame with 8 data rows at 30px
supporting.note: Confirms the intended composition: one 34px header row above N 30px data rows, columns 200px wide in the sample.

minHeight.note: Set explicitly. NOT derivable from the box model — see contractVsLocalCss, where the local stylesheet's 1+4+24+4+1 arithmetic requires a 4px vertical padding that Figma does not currently bind.

paddingInline.note: Figma's payload prints a 9px FALLBACK here. The export value of spacing/md is 8. Bind the token; the 9 is a codegen artefact.

paddingBlock.note: Figma's payload prints a 1px FALLBACK here. The export value of spacing/none is 0. DISAGREES with the local stylesheet, which binds spacing/sm (4) — see contractVsLocalCss.

border.note: 1px on ALL FOUR sides. Width is a raw literal; only the colour is tokenised.

frameWidth.note: Layout context, not a constraint. The sample layout uses 200px columns.

height.note: ⚠️ A FIXED height, not min-height — unlike the head cell and unlike every other measured component in this design system. A data cell therefore CANNOT grow for a long or wrapped value. Recorded as a defect, not normalised.

paddingInline.note: Fallback printed correctly as 8 here — unlike the head cell.

paddingBlock.note: Fallback printed correctly as 0 here — unlike the head cell.

truncation.value: single line, overflow hidden, text-ellipsis, white-space nowrap
truncation.note: Values truncate with an ellipsis — they never wrap. Consistent with the fixed height, and it means long content is silently cut with no tooltip recorded in the design.

composition.rule: One 34px head cell per column, above N 30px data cells. Borders are 1px on all four sides of every cell, so adjacent cells double up unless collapsed.
composition.note: The 1px-all-sides border on every cell is worth attention in implementation: without border-collapse or a negative-margin strategy, a table renders 2px internal gridlines. The design does not record which approach is intended.

letterSpacing.note: Binds fonts/tracking/X-tracking-0 — legacy name absent from the export. Correct name: fonts/tracking/tracking-0.

textTransform.note: NO uppercase treatment. The component set renders 'Title' in sentence case. Rendering header labels in CAPS is wrong against the design system — the local stylesheet reaches the same conclusion and verified it three independent ways.

fontSize.note: Figma's payload ALSO emits a raw text-[12px] on the same element, duplicating the token. Bind the token only.

typography.difference: Head and cell share size (12), line-height (16) and family. Only the WEIGHT differs — 500 for the header, 400 for the value.

colourFormula.pattern: The head cell uses surface/* and border/*; the data cell uses field/*. Both text colours use field/value-primary.

headText.note: A FIELD token used for header text — see namingException.

namingException.case: two token namespaces for one border, and field/* used for header text
namingException.detail: The head border binds border/subtle while the data-cell border binds field/border-default. BOTH resolve to #e2e8f0 — identical colour, two different token names, in one component family. Separately, the header's TEXT binds field/value-primary rather than a text/* token, even though the header is not a form field.
namingException.impact: No visual defect. But a generator inferring 'header uses border/*, cell uses field/*' will be right by accident, and a theme change to only one of the two namespaces would split a table's gridlines.

type.note: ONE variant each. No hover, no selected, no sorted-active, no zebra, no disabled, no error state exists on either set. Any such state built in code would be an invention — see notVerified.

contractVsLocalCss.status: ONE OPEN DISAGREEMENT — recorded, not silently resolved
contractVsLocalCss.localStylesheet: Universal Html Rules/02-components/table.css line 115 binds var(--spacing-sm) (4), commented '4 8 — the token values, NOT the payload's 9/5'.
contractVsLocalCss.consequence: Low visual impact — min-height 34 and align-items:center mean the label sits in the same place either way. But the local file's stated 34px arithmetic (1+4+24+4+1) REQUIRES the 4px padding; with Figma's current 0 the arithmetic gives 26 and the 34 comes from min-height alone.
contractVsLocalCss.whoIsRight: Not resolved here. Figma is the design authority and was measured today; the local file was written earlier from SPEC-08b and may predate a Figma edit. Needs the owner or Figma AI to confirm which is intended.
agreements: head min-height 34 and data-cell height 30 — both files agree exactly
1px border on all four sides — agree
text-transform: none on the header — agree, and the local file verified it three independent ways
the codegen fallback trap — the local file already documents it (it saw 9/5, this measurement saw 9/1), and both conclude: bind the token, never the printed fallback

defects: NO TABLE CONTRACT EXISTED IN THIS REPO UNTIL NOW, while the repo's only table stylesheet (src/styles/3-components/_tables.scss, 33 lines) contains ZERO height declarations. Every AI tool is instructed to read GitHub for component truth, so every tool asking 'how tall is a table row?' got no answer. This is the most likely cause of a feature session being unable to build tables to the design system.

TWO LIVE HEADER COMPONENTS, possibly three. This contract measures table_head 26938:61726; the document-level stylesheet builds 'Head / Tiltes for tables' 5865:162 and calls IT canonical; 'X-Head old' is a third, formally dead. Both live ones are 34px. Worse, section 26955:66556's own sample layout instantiates the OTHER header, not its own table_head set. See competingHeaderComponents.

The data cell uses a FIXED height:30 while the head cell uses min-height:34. Inconsistent mechanisms in one family, and the fixed height means a data cell cannot grow — it can only truncate. Every other component measured in this design system uses min-height.

Figma's generated payload prints WRONG padding fallbacks on the head cell: 9px where spacing/md is 8, and 1px where spacing/none is 0. The sibling data cell prints the same tokens correctly as 8 and 0. So the same two tokens print correctly in one component and incorrectly in the other.
Two token namespaces for the same border colour: head binds border/subtle, data cell binds field/border-default, both #e2e8f0.
The header's text colour binds field/value-primary — a FIELD token for a non-field element.
The data cell's value text carries a raw text-[12px] alongside the font-size/caption token that already sets it — a duplicated raw literal.
1px border on all four sides of EVERY cell, with no border-collapse strategy recorded. Rendered naively this produces 2px internal gridlines throughout a table.

The generated guidelines frame (26938:66226) reports its own annotation coverage as '0/2 — Incomplete' and 'No measurements added'. So the in-Figma guidelines for the table family are an empty shell — a tool reading them learns almost nothing.

That same guidelines frame's Dev Mode link points at node-id=26581-38709, which is NOT a table node — it is the same wrong link already recorded as a defect on the Fields contract. One broken link is being copied into generated guidelines.
fonts/tracking/X-tracking-0 bound on both text styles — legacy name, absent from the export. Correct name: fonts/tracking/tracking-0. This is now a SEVENTH component family with the same defect.

Only ONE variant exists on each set (type=Default). There is no hover, selected, sorted-active, zebra, disabled or error state anywhere in the table family, despite the head cell shipping an interactive Sort control and a help affordance.

openTokenDecision.gate: Design-owner approval required before any of these become bindings.
openTokenDecision.proposal: 1) Decide the head cell's vertical padding — spacing/none (Figma today) or spacing/sm (local stylesheet). 2) Change the data cell from height:30 to min-height:30 so a row can grow, matching the head cell and the rest of the system. 3) Settle one border namespace for the family. 4) Rename X-tracking-0 to tracking-0 (one Figma rename closes seven component families). 5) Consider whether 34 and 30 deserve real tokens — they are the two most repeated numbers in the product and are currently raw in both Figma and the local stylesheet. Note control/height-default = 30 already exists in Figma but not in the export, which may already cover the data-cell case.
openTokenDecision.untilApproved: Every affected value is published RAW with the disagreement recorded. Recording a value here is NOT permission to hardcode it.

The required/emergency icon (10495:19244) and help icon (10495:19340) beyond their 8px and 16px box sizes.

border-collapse / gridline strategy for an assembled table.

competingHeaderComponents.theTellingDetail: Section 26955:66556's own sample layout (27002:78668) instantiates nodes named 'Head / Tiltes for tables' (27002:78670, 27002:78681, 27002:78692) — the stylesheet's source — NOT its own table_head set. So the section that defines table_head does not use it in its own example.
competingHeaderComponents.consequence: Two live 34px header components with different names and node ids, plus one dead one. Any tool or person building a table must guess which to follow, and GitHub published none of them until today.
competingHeaderComponents.ask: Owner or Figma AI to declare one canonical header, and either retire or explicitly alias the other. Until then this contract measures table_head because that is the section the owner pointed at, and says so rather than implying it is the only one.
